tagline: Seasonal food, cooked over a wood fire.

intro.title: Cinder, where the evening slows down.
intro.text: A wood-fire kitchen in Heidelberg's old town. We cook what the farms of the Rhine-Neckar bring us each week, let the embers do most of the work, and pour wines from the slopes you can see from the river.

images.alt: Chef flambéing in a pan over open flames
Chef pouring sauce over a plated dish

menuFeature.title: Flavours that wait for the embers.
menuFeature.text: Nothing here is rushed. Beef cheek braises for twelve hours, beetroot roasts whole in the ashes, and every sauce reduces until it tastes of the fire it came from. The menu changes with the week, never with the trend.
menuFeature.imageAlt: Beef fillet in pastry, sliced on a dark plate

fire.title: One fire. Lit at noon, never rushed.
fire.text: Beech and oak from the Odenwald. No gas, no shortcuts. By the time you sit down, the embers have been working for hours.
fire.imageAlt: Chef cooking over open flames in a dark kitchen

privateDining.title: Your evening, your menu.
privateDining.text: Birthdays, team dinners, weddings. Up to 36 guests at one long table, with a menu we build around you.
privateDining.imageAlt: Long dinner table set with flowers and candles in a dark room

about.title: Hospitality that feels like coming home.
about.text: Cinder sits in a 300-year-old vaulted room a few steps from the Old Bridge. Thick walls, low light, one long bar. We wanted a place where you can come for a full tasting menu or just a glass of wine and a plate of bread, and feel equally welcome.
about.imageAlt: Vaulted dining room with a small window and set tables
